description: A mathematically-inclined Data Science major who is confident in logic and algorithmic theory but apprehensive about the technical shift from Python to C++ memory management.

nodes.description: Detailed introduction to C++ pointers and references, focusing on memory addressing compared to high-level references in Python or Java.
nodes.title: Pointers and References in C++
nodes.personalizationRationale: This student has no_prior_exposure to C++, requiring foundational scaffolding to bridge the gap from high-level memory management to manual pointer logic.

nodes.description: Overview of the C++ compilation model, including header files (.h), source files (.cpp), and the role of the linker.
nodes.title: C++ Project Structure and Compilation
nodes.personalizationRationale: As the student has no_prior_exposure to C++, scaffolding on the header-source file separation is essential for achieving lab parity with peers.

nodes.description: Deep dive into stack vs. heap allocation, using the 'new' and 'delete' operators to manage dynamic memory.
nodes.title: Manual Memory Management and Dynamic Allocation
nodes.personalizationRationale: Addressing the student's no_prior_exposure tier, this node introduces manual memory management to prevent early bottlenecks in building custom structures.
Core requirement for designing reusable data structure interfaces as specified in the course syllabus.
nodes.title: Classes and Inheritance in C++
nodes.description: Implementation of C++ classes, including constructors, destructors, and inheritance hierarchies for object-oriented design.

nodes.title: Templates and Exception Handling
nodes.description: Utilizing C++ templates for generic programming and implementing robust error handling with exceptions.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential core competency for building generic, reusable containers required for all students.
Standard core content for Week 3, focusing on fundamental sequential data structure implementation.
nodes.description: Implementation and manipulation of singly and doubly linked lists within the C++ environment.
nodes.title: Linked List Implementation

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory assessment checkpoint (Quiz 1) to evaluate the student's understanding of recursive logic and complexity.
nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion and Analysis
nodes.description: Assessment covering recursion depth and asymptotic notation (Big-O) analysis of early algorithms.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Required core syllabus content on sequence-based structures essential for mid-course mastery.
nodes.description: Implementation of Stack and Queue ADTs using the C++ Standard Template Library (STL).
nodes.title: Stacks, Queues, and Deques

nodes.description: Detailed study of dynamic arrays (vectors), amortized analysis of growth, and the use of iterators.
nodes.title: Vectors and Iterators
nodes.personalizationRationale: Foundational core topic regarding sequence container efficiency and navigation.
Core requirement for understanding early sorting algorithms and their limitations in sequential structures.
nodes.description: Introduction to sequence sorting through the Bubble Sort algorithm and its performance characteristics.
nodes.title: Sequences and Bubble Sort

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory midterm-review assessment covering the first three blocks of required material.
nodes.title: Midterm Review Assessment
nodes.description: Comprehensive review of material from C++ foundations through sequence-based structures in preparation for the midterm.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential core requirement for processing non-linear hierarchical data.
nodes.title: General Trees and Traversals
nodes.description: Study of general tree structures and the implementation of Pre-order, Post-order, and In-order traversals.

nodes.title: Binary Tree Properties
nodes.description: Properties and implementations of binary trees, including mathematical bounds on height and node count.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard core topic necessary for understanding advanced search tree structures.
Mandatory core block content focusing on efficient selection and order maintenance.
nodes.title: Priority Queues and Heaps
nodes.description: Implementation of heaps and their application in providing efficient priority queue interfaces.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core associative container topic including the mandatory Quiz 3 assessment checkpoint.
nodes.description: Implementation of hash functions and collision resolution strategies, including a formal quiz on maps and skip lists.
nodes.title: Maps, Hash Tables, and Quiz 3

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core theoretical and practical requirement for understanding balanced search structures.
nodes.title: Binary Search and AVL Trees
nodes.description: In-depth analysis of Binary Search Trees (BST) and the implementation of AVL tree rotations for balance.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Required theory-heavy content for advanced data structures mastery in the course.
nodes.title: Red-Black and Multi-Way Trees
nodes.description: Introduction to Multi-way search trees, including (2,4) trees and Red-Black tree properties.
Detailed comparison of Merge Sort and Selection Sort, focusing on time and space complexity.
nodes.title: Merge and Selection Sort Analysis
nodes.personalizationRationale: Capstone sorting content required for the final examination and comparative algorithm analysis.

nodes.description: Comprehensive review of the entire syllabus, concluding with Quiz 4 and final exam preparation.
nodes.title: Final Cumulative Course Review
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory final assessment checkpoint covering the entire cumulative curriculum.
